workload: Walk every calendar day from 1990-01-01 to 2070-01-01 by calling add_days(1), thirty times. That is the inner step of date_range(..., '1D') and of daily schedule generation.
notes: add_days is about 95% of the walk. For a scalar step it returns Date.from_excel(self.excel_dt + n). from_excel splits off a zero time-of-day and then Date.__init__ re-validates the month and recomputes the Excel serial that was just supplied; that reconstruction is about three quarters of the walk. Whole-day steps can return Date._make_fast from ymd_from_excel, which this file already uses for IMM dates, and leave a fractional serial on the current path so intraday dates stay identical. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median across 7 process runs. Checksum of day numbers was 459620 on every run.

workload: Mark each weekday from 2000-01-03 through 2040-01-02 (10,435 dates, built before the timer) as a TARGET business day via is_business_day, twenty times. EUR swap schedules and get_holiday_list do this.
notes: holiday_target is about three quarters of that scan. Every call builds Easter Monday through easter_monday (a new Date) and add_days(-3) (another Date) only to compare them with dt. The Easter Monday Excel serial is a year-indexed table plus a day offset. Cache that serial on the calendar and compare dt.excel_dt with the cached Good Friday and Easter Monday serials; the fixed month/day holidays stay as they are, so the booleans do not change. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median across 7 process runs. Every run counted 194 holidays.

workload: Dirty-price 150 fixed-coupon US bonds (maturities 2027-2056, five coupons) off one 40-year flat-forward discount curve, forty times. Curve and bonds are built before the timer.
notes: The timed section is entirely dirty_price_from_discount_curve, and about 87% of it is one DiscountCurve.df call per remaining cashflow. Each scalar df rebuilds a one-element time array and re-wraps the knot arrays inside interpolate. df already accepts a list of dates and, on this curve, a single vector call per bond reproduced the scalar dirty price to 1e-14. Keep the ex-dividend and redemption rules in the cashflow loop and discount the resulting flows in one call. The native test prices a coupon bond off a discount curve to 4 decimals via clean_price_from_discount_curve. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median across 7 process runs. The price checksum was identical on every run.

workload: Price one 1-year American put (spot 100, strike 100, vol 20%, r 5%, q 2%) with EquityBinomialTree.value at 3000 steps. value calls _value_once at 3000 and 3001 steps. A 32-step call warms numba first; the metric is the steady-state pricing call, not compile time.
notes: The metric is the increase in Linux ru_maxrss, in bytes, across that pricing call. _value_once allocates stock_values and option_values of length n(n+1)/2. For the larger call (3001 steps) those two float64 grids are 72,120,048 bytes, which is 99.9% of the measured high-water increase. Delta, gamma, and theta only read the nodes on the first two time layers, so backward induction can keep two length-(n+1) layers and recompute those stock prices from the CRR formula. The unit tests compare price, delta, gamma, and theta after rounding to 3 decimals. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median across 7 process runs. The reported price was 6.6682007897 on every run.
